title: Access and eligibility gates
description: Canonical wire identifiers for the separately-evaluated access checks (INV-030, INV-031). RCE-053. PROPOSAL PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION: this enum carries SIX identifiers, not five. ADR-006 lists 'Account access' first; README.md and QUALITY.md both list 'real-user eligibility' in that slot. DOMAIN.md backs them with two different records — UserAccount (identity binding, status, settings) and UserEligibility (assurance status, method, result, expiry, policy version) — so folding them into one identifier would change meaning rather than spelling. See docs/implementation/CONTRACTS.md for the mapping and evidence. If the owner confirms five, delete real_user_assurance and remap its row; that is a one-value change.

GateId.description: account_access: the principal is authenticated and authorized for this resource. real_user_assurance: the real person behind the account has satisfied the age-assurance policy. fictional_adult_eligibility: the character's age is known and adult. player_content_authorization: the player's own content opt-in, outside fiction. character_current_willingness: the character's scoped, revocable in-fiction willingness. provider_capability: what the model adapter actually permits.

GateOutcome.description: 'unknown' denies. A gate that cannot be evaluated is never treated as satisfied (INV-005, INV-030).

GateDenialReason.description: Stable reasons. Deliberately never includes preference, orientation, relationship status, relationship history, bodily response, repeated past action or silence — none of those may deny or satisfy any gate (INV-031).

GateReport.description: Every gate is reported, always, so a caller can never mistake an unevaluated gate for a satisfied one. A report is authoritative only for the moment it was evaluated; willingness in particular is rechecked at execution and at commit (INV-033).

permitted.description: True only when every evaluation is 'satisfied'. A convenience for callers; never a substitute for the individual outcomes.
